edges.description: Defective maturation and activation across T, B, NK and innate lymphoid lineages gives a combined immune deficiency.

Infection susceptibility follows from defective lymphocyte maturation. In the largest cohort the respiratory infections are attributed substantially to epilepsy and aspiration rather than to the immune defect alone, so the two routes are not separable from these data.

Three of seven patients in the Finnish and Omani cohort developed B-cell lymphoma. The cohort reporting a DNA-repair defect raises genome maintenance as a contributing route, but neither the defective B-cell maturation nor the repair defect has been shown to be the operative mechanism.
The knockout does not produce the reduced brain size that defines the human cortical phenotype, although it does show a ventricular abnormality.
edges.limitations: Grossly normal body and brain size means the defining human feature is absent. ClinGen records the same discrepancy for the mouse models generally, noting they did not reproduce the microcephaly, seizures or cortical blindness while reproducing the immune phenotype. Mammalian formin redundancy with mDia2 and mDia3 and species differences in cortical neurogenesis are candidate explanations and neither is tested in the cited work.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous nonsense, frameshift and canonical splice-site DIAPH1 variants remove functional mDia1. ClinGen records loss of function as the mechanism of pathogenicity for this entity, in explicit contrast to the gain-of-function mechanism of the dominant DIAPH1 hearing-loss arm. A heterozygous truncating allele that removes the FH2 domain abolishes actin-elongation activity in vitro, which is the direct biochemical demonstration that truncation destroys the protein's catalytic output.

nodes.description: The same adhesion and microtubule-organizing-center defect in lymphocytes produces poor lymphocyte activation and proliferation, defective B-cell maturation and a lack of naive T cells. CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of DIAPH1 in healthy-donor peripheral blood mononuclear cells reproduces the T-cell activation defect, which makes this the most directly demonstrated branch of the mechanism. In the largest cohort the gross lymphocyte subsets and serum immunoglobulins were usually normal while T-cell receptor excision circles and naive T-lymphocyte counts were consistently low, so the laboratory signature is thymic output rather than lymphopenia.

nodes.description: The cell-biological consequence shared by every organ affected: loss of mDia1 impairs establishment of cell polarity, mitotic spindle formation and cell division, and repositioning of the microtubule-organizing center. In human neuronal precursor cells mDia1 is expressed during mitotic division and has a major effect on spindle formation; in patient T cells the same lesion leaves the microtubule-organizing center unable to reposition efficiently to the immunologic synapse. This is the node at which the neural and immune branches separate.

nodes.description: mDia1 is expressed in human neuronal precursor cells during mitotic division and is required for normal spindle formation, so its loss distorts progenitor division during corticogenesis and lowers cortical neuron output. The resulting microcephaly is postnatal and progressive rather than congenital, and the structural abnormalities reported across the largest cohort are frequently occipital-predominant, which is consistent with the cortical visual impairment that accompanies them. The step from a demonstrated human-precursor spindle defect to the cortical phenotype is an inference: no human neurodevelopmental tissue or organoid study of DIAPH1 loss is cited in the sources used here, and the mouse knockout does not reproduce the microcephaly.

nodes.description: mDia1 is a Diaphanous-related formin and a Rho effector. On binding GTP-bound Rho its autoinhibition is relieved and the FH2 domain nucleates and processively elongates long linear actin filaments, which is the activity that maintains polarity during adhesion, migration and cell division. Loss of mDia1 removes that activity.
